faqs.question: How do I make a Diwali gift box at home?
faqs.answer: Pick a rigid box one size larger than the biggest item, line the food corner with butter paper, seal each sweet in its own lidded tub, then lay filler, heavy items, non-food items in a separate bag, more filler and the card on top. A three-tub box takes about 90 minutes of packing once the sweets are made.

faqs.question: Can I wrap homemade sweets in newspaper for a gift?
faqs.answer: No. FSSAI's Packaging Regulations, 2018 (regulation 3(11)) say newspaper or any such material shall not be used for storing and wrapping food, because printing ink is not meant to touch what you eat. Use butter paper, foil or a food-grade tub instead.

faqs.question: How long will homemade sweets stay fresh in a gift box?
faqs.answer: It depends on the sweet and the wrap. A 2025 Scientific Reports study found Mohanthal stayed acceptable up to 20 days at 30 °C in laminates or polystyrene tubs but 16 days in cardboard boxes or LDPE pouches; milk sweets keep far less and should stay refrigerated until handover.

faqs.question: Can I reuse an old dry-fruit or biscuit tin for my Diwali hamper?
faqs.answer: Use it for the diyas, candles or decorations, not the sweets. FSSAI's 2018 packaging regulations say tin containers once used shall not be re-used for packaging food, and the rule is a sensible yardstick at home too.

faqs.question: What filler stops things moving inside a hamper?
faqs.answer: Shredded kraft paper works well: a 2–3 cm base layer, then more tucked around the tubs until a 45-degree tilt makes no sliding sound. About 100 g fills 3–4 boxes and costs roughly ₹60–120 EST (Oct 2026).

faqs.question: How much does it cost to make a DIY Diwali hamper?
faqs.answer: A three-tub box with homemade sweets comes to roughly ₹600–1,200 EST (October 2026), ingredients included. That is the writer's estimate, not a shop-checked price, and it varies by city and by what goes in.

faqs.question: How early can I pack a Diwali box for 29 October 2027?
faqs.answer: Box, liner, tubs, filler and non-food items can be ready a week ahead, by Friday 22 October 2027. Dry besan or dry-fruit sweets can go in on 26–27 October, and milk sweets should be made on Thursday 28 October, chilled, and added on the day.

faqs.question: Do I need an FSSAI licence to give homemade sweets as gifts?
faqs.answer: FSSAI's packaging rules are written for food businesses, and a one-off gift from your own kitchen is not a business. If you start selling boxes you become one, so check FSSAI's registration requirements before taking orders.

faqs.question: Is a handmade hamper really valued more than a bought one?
faqs.answer: Not by everyone. Research summarised in The Conversation in January 2025 found the handmade label raised felt love and willingness to pay only for people who like to deliberate, and backfired for action-first 'doers'.

faqs.question: Can I put a digital Diwali card inside a physical gift box?
faqs.answer: Yes. Print the link to a SubhSandesh Diwali page as a QR code on the card that sits on top of the box. With 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages opened on a phone, print it large on matte card so a phone camera reads it.

article.contentMarkdown:
# DIY Diwali Gift Box: Packing a Homemade Hamper That Stays Fresh

A DIY Diwali gift box holds up when you pack it in a fixed order: a rigid box, a food-grade liner, each homemade sweet sealed in its own lidded tub, heavy items low, filler in every gap, and the card on top. Plan it backwards from Lakshmi Puja on Friday 29 October 2027, because festival gifts get left late.

In SubhSandesh's own Raksha Bandhan 2026 data, our nearest festival analogue and a small sample of 89 pages, 49.4% were built on the festival day itself and 27.0% the day before. If you add a link card, 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, so the card must scan from one.

Below: seven packing steps with estimated costs, FSSAI's 2018 rules on newspaper and reused tins, a 2025 study on which wrap keeps mithai longest, and a Diwali 2027 calendar.

## What a DIY Diwali gift box is, and its 3 layers

A DIY Diwali gift box is a hamper you assemble yourself from a plain box, homemade or bought items and filler, instead of buying a sealed one. It has three layers: the outer box, the wrap that touches food, and the filler that stops things moving.

The [Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Regulations, 2018](https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Gazette_Notification_Packaging_03_01_2019.pdf), notified by FSSAI on 24 December 2018, draw the same line: material touching food is "primary" packaging, the layer around it "secondary". The tub around the ladoos is the layer worth the care.

## 7 steps to assemble a DIY Diwali gift box, in packing order

Each step gives the job, the reason, a cost and the time. Costs are the writer's estimates for October 2026, marked EST and not shop-checked.

### 1. Choose a rigid box one size larger than the biggest item

A corrugated kraft or rigid board box of about 10 × 10 × 4 inches takes two sweet tubs, a small jar and two diyas without crushing anything. Size it to the tallest item plus 2 cm of filler, so the lid closes flat. EST ₹60–150 per box (Oct 2026); about 10 minutes.

### 2. Line the food corner with grease-proof or butter paper

Painted card, chart paper and printed boxes should not touch food; the 2018 regulations say a printed surface "shall not come into direct contact with food products". One sheet of butter paper solves it. EST ₹80–150 for a roll that lines 8–10 boxes (Oct 2026); about 5 minutes.

### 3. Seal each homemade sweet in its own lidded tub

Put each sweet type in its own lidded food-grade tub so flavours stay apart. Cool sweets fully before closing, because trapped steam becomes moisture. EST ₹15–30 per 500 ml polypropylene tub (Oct 2026); about 15 minutes for three.

### 4. Lay the base filler, then the heaviest items flat on it

Spread a 2–3 cm bed of shredded kraft paper and set the tubs and any glass jar on it, lids up. Heavy-low and light-high means a tilted box shifts paper, not glass. EST ₹60–120 for 100 g of shredded paper, enough for 3–4 boxes (Oct 2026); about 5 minutes.

### 5. Bag diyas, candles and agarbatti away from the food

Wax, incense and diya oil carry smells, and ghee-rich sweets pick them up. Seal non-food items in their own bag and place them farthest from the tubs. EST ₹100–250 for two clay diyas and a small candle (Oct 2026); about 5 minutes.

### 6. Fill every gap until nothing slides when you tilt the box

Tuck filler around the tubs until a 45-degree tilt makes no sliding sound. Keep shedding dried marigold outside the food bags. Cost is a handful more of the step 4 filler; about 5 minutes.

### 7. Put the card on top and list the contents on its back

The card goes in last, flat under the lid, so it is seen first. On its back, list each sweet with the day it was made, so the recipient knows what to eat first. EST ₹20–60 for a blank card (Oct 2026); about 10 minutes.

Added up, a three-tub box with homemade sweets comes to roughly ₹600–1,200 EST (Oct 2026), ingredients included. Packing takes about 90 minutes once the sweets are made.

## FSSAI's 2018 packaging rules, applied to a homemade box

The 2018 regulations bind food businesses, which had until 1 July 2019 to comply; a home kitchen packing a gift is not one. They remain the clearest official yardstick, and four lines map onto a DIY box:

- **No newspaper.** "Newspaper or any such material shall not be used for storing and wrapping of food" (regulation 3(11)), so no newspaper lining under ladoos either.
- **No second life for tins.** "Tin containers once used, shall not be re-used for packaging of food" (3(7)). The old dry-fruit tin can carry the diyas instead.
- **No print on food.** A printed surface must not touch food directly (3(10)), which is why step 2 exists.
- **No recycled plastic bags.** Recycled-plastic products, carry bags included, "shall not be used for packaging, storing, carrying or dispensing articles of food".

Schedule IV of the notification suggests packaging for sweets, including metal containers with polypropylene caps, lidded paper-board or foil containers and rigid plastic containers. A lidded tub fits that list; loose sweets on a paper doily do not. The clauses are quoted as notified in December 2018, and later amendments were not traced.

## Which wrap keeps mithai longest: a 2025 Mohanthal study

A [2025 study in Scientific Reports](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12700949) stored Mohanthal, a sweet of besan, ghee, khoa and sugar syrup, in four packagings at 30 °C. Laminates and polystyrene tubs kept it acceptable for up to 20 days, against 16 days for cardboard boxes and LDPE pouches. Cardboard lost the most moisture, and cardboard and LDPE showed more fat oxidation.

The panel's overall acceptability score fell from 8.02 fresh to 6.66 by day 20, and the authors stress hygiene during cooling and packing to keep yeast and mould out. So a sweet laid straight into cardboard goes stale sooner than one in a lidded tub. The figures cover one ghee-rich sweet in a laboratory; milk-heavy sweets such as kalakand belong in the fridge until handover.

## A Diwali 2027 packing calendar, set against when people actually build

Diwali 2027 runs from Dhanteras on Wednesday 27 October to Bhai Dooj on Sunday 31 October, with Lakshmi Puja on Friday 29 October. The table maps each packing window to its tasks, beside the share of SubhSandesh Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages built in the matching window. That is a different festival and only 89 pages, so read the last column as a warning about last-minute habits, not a Diwali forecast.

| Packing window, Diwali 2027 | What to do then | Raksha Bandhan 2026 pages built in that window (n = 89) |
|---|---|---|
| 4+ days ahead, by Mon 25 Oct | Buy box, liner, tubs and filler; make dry snacks such as shakarpara | 6.7% |
| 2–3 days ahead, Tue 26 – Wed 27 Oct | Make besan or dry-fruit sweets; bag the non-food items | 5.6% |
| Day before, Thu 28 Oct | Make milk sweets and chill them; assemble the box without them | 27.0% |
| The day, Fri 29 Oct | Add the chilled tubs, close the box, write the card | 49.4% |

If you are in that 49.4%, front-load everything that does not spoil, leaving only the tubs for the last 24 hours. Another 11.2% of those rakhi pages came after the festival had passed, the group an early-packed box rescues.

## Does a handmade box mean more to the person who gets it?

It depends on the person. In a 2025 study its authors summarised in [The Conversation on 22 January 2025](https://theconversation.com/does-made-with-love-sell-research-reveals-who-values-handmade-products-the-most-247351), people choosing a gift for a loved one felt more "love" in a mug labelled handmade and would pay more, but only those who like to deliberate. For action-first "doers" the label backfired, and they felt more love for an unlabelled mug.

A [2023 paper in Psychology & Marketing](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mar.21812) found a similar reversal in people whose sense of personal control had been shaken, and the effect eased when they could customise the product. Only its abstract was read. So match the box to the recipient: tell the story on the card for an aunt who plans everything, and keep it practical for a rushed friend.

## Where a SubhSandesh Diwali page fits inside the box

A box carries a card, but not photos or a song. SubhSandesh's [interactive Diwali card with diyas, rangoli and a shagun liffafa](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) is a private link where the recipient lights a diya at their door and a row of wish diyas, colours a rangoli with your initials and opens your letter from a red-and-gold liffafa. It holds up to six photos in sky lanterns and takes about five minutes to make, so print its link as a QR code on the step 7 card.

Shared SubhSandesh pages average 11.1 views each, so a link tends to be reopened after the sweets are gone. With 48.3% of views on a phone, print the QR large, on matte card, so a phone camera reads it.

For a partner who enjoys working for a surprise, a [photo jigsaw whose final piece is not in the box](https://subhsandesh.in/photo-puzzle) suits the card instead. Either is a greeting for one person, not a packing tool.

## When a DIY box is the wrong choice, and where SubhSandesh loses

A homemade box is the wrong call in four cases:

- **The box travels more than a day.** Milk sweets should not ride unrefrigerated; pack dry sweets only, or send a shop-sealed box.
- **You need 20 boxes for an office.** At about 90 minutes each, that is 30 hours of packing; a bought hamper wins.
- **Someone has an allergy or strict diet.** List every ingredient on the card, nuts and ghee included, or leave food out.
- **Your kitchen is chaos in Diwali week.** The Mohanthal authors' mould warning applies at home too.

SubhSandesh loses with a recipient who never uses a phone camera; a handwritten note works better there. Nor can it replace the food: an elderly neighbour wants the ladoo, not a link.

- Chaudhary et al., [Packaging materials and the shelf life of Mohanthal](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12700949), Scientific Reports, 23 November 2025.
- Degirmenci, Mortimer and Mathmann, [Does 'made with love' sell?](https://theconversation.com/does-made-with-love-sell-research-reveals-who-values-handmade-products-the-most-247351), The Conversation, 22 January 2025.
- Song, He and Jiang, [The negative handmade effect](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mar.21812), Psychology & Marketing, 27 March 2023 (abstract only).
